trust_decision.summary: Interval::poll_tick decides that the timer entry is no longer referenced by the time driver because its state reads 'elapsed', and then frees it without taking the driver lock. But the driver publishes the elapsed state before it finishes touching the entry (take_waker), so the timer memory is released or reused while the driver thread still accesses it.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names tokio::time::Interval, and poll_tick holds the only `unsafe` call, with the comment 'SAFETY: the internal timer is elapsed'.

fix_sites.entry_point: drop of tokio::time::Sleep (sleep/sleep_until/timeout); the fix removes the Sleep-level PinnedDrop cancel
Sleep::reset_without_timer, pub(super), reached only from Interval::poll_tick
crate-internal runtime::Timer enum (dispatches between the traditional and alt flavours)
TimerEntry (the fix adds an owned driver handle and a PinnedDrop that cancels)
time_alt::Timer (the fix adds Drop that cancels; tokio_unstable + rt-multi-thread only)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: tokio/src/runtime/time_alt/timer.rs:43-45 (alternative timer wheel; the published fix adds Drop->cancel here too)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The alt timer is gated behind tokio_unstable and rt-multi-thread (tokio/src/runtime/mod.rs:459), and its EntryHandle is lock-protected and refcounted (tokio/src/runtime/time_alt/entry.rs:246-264), so dropping it without cancel looks like a leak rather than memory unsafety.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: After poll_tick returns Ready, it must not register a timer or waker. The next tick is registered lazily on the next poll, and the tests check that a stream stalls when it does not re-wake. Re-registering eagerly, for example by calling Sleep::reset instead of dropping the timer, would break this. The lock-free extend_expiration fast path in reset must also stay.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: reset_immediately (or reset_at with a past deadline) implemented through reset_without_timer to skip registering a timer that is already due
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same 'do not register yet, it will be registered on next poll' optimisation as poll_tick, plausibly justified by a 'SAFETY: deadline already passed' comment

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Timer::reset Alternative branch replacing the entry with entry.set(...) without the preceding cancel()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The new entry overwrites the old one, so cancel looks redundant to a maintainer optimising reset

O8b_injection_room.sibling: this.timer.set(Some(timer)) reached while a previous elapsed timer is still Some (e.g. a 're-arm after Ready' path in poll_elapsed)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A re-arm after Ready would be tempting for periodic users. It would be the same 'state reads elapsed, so the driver is done' assumption, without taking the lock

O9_family: race condition / premature release of driver-shared intrusive timer memory (CWE-362, use-after-free class)

O10_build.toolchain: cargo, rust-version 1.85 (tokio/Cargo.toml); loom for the published regression test (cfg loom)
O10_build.project_tests: tokio/src/runtime/time/tests/mod.rs (loom model tests; the fix adds interval_poll_tick_races_with_fire), tokio/tests/time_interval.rs, tokio/tests/time_sleep.rs

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Call timer.cancel(driver) inside Sleep::reset_without_timer before set(None). This is a one-line fix that is in fact sufficient, because it takes the driver lock. So the task collapses to a single location.

out_of_scope_notes: tokio/CHANGELOG.md:40 names the regressing change ('time: remove the runtime handle from timers' #8458), so a solver with git history can simply revert it. Strip history and the changelog line in our copy.
